parsed.explanation: Combined regime is split and contested: one region has no consensual same-sex offence, the other may retain a 10-14 year ordinance, reach trans people via public morality, and gives no discrimination recourse. Undated but documented police arrests and torture of gay residents on collaboration grounds, two explicit prosecutions, banned LGBTQ activity and subsequent hate threats, low social acceptance and harsher family/social persecution make outing potentially severe, while no trans-specific criminal ban, detention practice, screening, facilities or dated trans violence is documented. Thin, undated data extrapolate toward risk, not midpoint, but do not support routine trans imprisonment/execution.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport, visa, marker and screening practice not documented; visitor could enter either legal region.
entry_documents.protection: One region derives from code with no consensual same-sex offence; no trans entry ban documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document presentation could encounter contested 1936 ordinance or public-morality provisions depending on itinerary.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Spokesperson reports police arrested and tortured gay residents, usually on collaboration charges; two explicit homosexuality trials in undated three-year window. No trans detention placement documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Morality/collaboration allegations could convert discovery into custody; foreigner/consular access not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Bathroom, ward and facility access not documented. Shared-regime split documented, not facility practice.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Unknown facility practice interacts with public-morality risk if outed in facilities.

care_services.exposure: HIV medication interrupted by scarcity/stigma; blockaded region health collapse since Oct 2023 makes life-saving medication especially hard to obtain. HRT/emergency access not documented.
care_services.interaction: Care disruption compounds custody/social exposure, especially in blockaded region.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Contested 1936 ordinance: 10 years consensual carnal knowledge, 14 years with child; public-morality provisions said to reach trans people. Police banned LGBTQ activity; hate wave followed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No broad anti-discrimination protection documented; domestic LGR absence is resident-facing only.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Contested text plus documented enforcement gives police an operative lever despite legal uncertainty.

minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. No age-dependent rule, family accompaniment protection or minor-specific exposure is sourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Periodic transphobic threats/attacks reported without dates/counts; family/public discrimination and abuse reported in 2018 women-only sample; low acceptance rank 130th through 2020. No trans-specific rate documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police banned LGBTQ activity; no documented protective response to hate messages.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social/family persecution described as harsher than formal law; recourse not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No functioning remedy documented; 2003 draft code status unknown; ordinance applicability contested among monitors; treaty gaps unnamed.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Legal uncertainty plus absence of recourse prevents relying on the more permissive region's text.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.15: no documented routine trans arrests, months-long custody, beatings of trans visitors, or credible lethal pathway; torture report concerns gay residents, is undated, and explicit prosecutions were rare (two).

Lower than 0.35: police harm here is reported as torture not hours-long detention/fines, possible penalty is up to 10-14 years, and no working complaint remedy is documented, whereas 0.35 rarely escalates to imprisonment.

Similar to 0.25: severe custodial/social exposure and thin recourse, but trans-specific custody placement, assault frequency and birth-sex housing are not documented, and criminalisation is contested rather than established.

parsed.synthesis: If outed, the traveller faces an uncertain mix of permissive and potentially 10-year criminal texts, public-morality reach, documented police torture in analogous gay cases, banned organising, unaddressed hate threats, hostile family/social conditions and disrupted HIV care, with no documented remedy. No trans-specific ban, capital practice, routine trans detention or dated trans attack rate is proven, so this is not the 0.15 tier; documented custodial severity keeps it below 0.35.
